Daily Quiz.question: ১) In what year did Shakespeare die?
Daily Quiz.exp:
William Shakespeare is the greatest English dramatist.
He was born on 23 April, 1564 AD, and died on 23 April, 1616 AD.
His Birthplace is Stratford Avon. He is often called the Bard of Avon.
Shakespearean period belongs to '1590-1616'.
He wrote 37 plays and 154 sonnets.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ২) Who wrote the the book 'All for Love'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
John Dryden is the Father of Modern English Criticism.
His famous works are:
All for Love, The Indian Emperor, Aureng-Zebe, The Mistaken Husband, Absalom and Achitophel, MacFlecknoe, The essay of Dramatic Poesy, The Conquest of Granada, The Medal of John Bays.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ৩) The first English tragedy is-
Daily Quiz.exp:
- Gorboduc, the first English tragedy, is written by Thomas Norton and Thomas Sackville.
- Ralph Roister Doister, the first Comedy in English, is written by Nicholas Udall.
- The Faerie Queene is a famous epic of Edmund Spencer.
- Pamela or Virtue Rewarded, the first English novel, is written by Samuel Richardson.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ৪) Who wrote the book 'Novum Orgamum'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Francis Bacon is called natural philosopher. He is also called the Father of English Essay and Father of Modern Prose.
His famous works are Essays, Advancement of Learning, Novum Orgamum, The Wisdom of Ancients, Divine and Humane and The New Atlantis etc.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ৫) Who is the father of modern English Poetry?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Geoffrey Chaucer is the father of modern English Poetry.
His best writings are Canterbury Tales, Troilus and Criseyde.
He is also called Father of English Language, Father of English literature, First Humourist in English Literature, The First great Modernist.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ৬) Who wrote the novel 'A Tale of a Tub'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Jonathan Swift is the greatest satirist of the 18th century.
His famous works are Gulliver's Travels, A tale of a Tub, The Battle of the Books, A Modest Proposal, A Journey to Stella.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ৭) Who wrote the world-famous tragedy 'Antony and Cleopatra'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Famous Tragedies of William Shakespeare are Hamlet, Macbeth, Othello, King Lear, Julius Caesar, Romeo and Juliet, Antony and Cleopatra, Titus Andronicus, Timon of Athens.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopedia of Britanncia.

Daily Quiz.question: ৮) Who is the writer of 'An Essay on Criticism'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Alexander Pope is called Mock Heroic Poet.
His famous works are An Essay on Criticism, The Dunciad, The Imitation of Horace, An Essay on Man, Letter to Gay.
Famous epics of Alexander Pope is 'The Rape of the Lock'.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ৯) Who wrote the play 'Volpone'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Ben Jonson is called a neo-classicist because he followed the classical rules of drama: Every Man in His Humour, Every Man Out of His Humour.
‌‌ His comedies are known as 'Comedy of Humors'.
His famous works are The Magnetic Lady, Volpone, The Silent Woman, The Alchemist, The Devil is an Ass etc.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১০) Who wrote the novel 'Tom Jones'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Henry Fielding regarded as 'Father of English Novel'.
His famous novels are Tom Jones, Amelia, Joseph Andrews, Jonathan Wilde, Top Secret.
His famous plays are Rape Upon Rape, The Temple Beau, The Tragedy of Tragedies, The Modern Husband.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১১) Who of the following is a University Wit?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Elizabethan Period এর একদল Young dramatist and pamphleteers (ক্ষুদ্র পুস্তিকা রচয়িতা) দেরকে University Wits বলা হয়।
তাঁরা Oxford and Cambridge University এর Scholar/Witty students ছিলেন। তাঁরা অনেক বিখ্যাত নাটক রচনা ও মঞ্চস্থ করার মাধ্যমে খ্যাতি অর্জন করেছিলেন। University Wits ছিলেন মোট ৭ জন।
এঁরা হলেন- Christopher Marlowe, Thomas Kyd, Robert Greene, George Peele, Thomas Nashe, John Lyly and Thomas Lodge.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ১২) Who is the writer of 'The Jew of Malta'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Christopher Marlowe is the Father of English Tragedy. He is the greatest Dramatist before William Shakespeare.
His famous Tragedies are Doctor Faustus, The Jew of Malta, Tambeurlaine the Great, Edward II, The Massacre of Paris etc.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৩) Who is called 'Epic Poet'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
John Milton is called 'Epic Poet' and 'A great master of verse in Puritan Period'.
His famous epics are Paradise Lost and Paradise Regained.
His famous books are Comus, Lycidas, Of Education and Areopagitica.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৪) Who is the writer of the novel 'Arcadia'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Sir Philip Sidney is a famous critic, poet and soldier.
His famous books are Arcadia (A book that bears the embryo of English Novel), The Lady of May, An Apology for Poetry.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৫) Who is called Poet of Love and Religious Poet?
Daily Quiz.exp:
John Donne is a Metaphysical Poet.
He is called Poet of Love and Religious Poet.
His famous works are The Good Morrow, The Sun Rising, The Canonization, Twicknam Garden, For Whom The Bell Tolls, The Anatomy of the World (book), The Frea, The Ecstasy, The Funeral etc.
Source: Live MCQ lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৬) 'The Faerie Queen' is written by-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Edmund Spenser is called the poet of poets.
His notable works are The Faerie Queen (Epic), the Shepherds Calendar, The Ruins of Time.
His famous sonnet collection is Amoretti.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৭) Who is famous for the objective presentation of deep knowledge about human psychology?
Daily Quiz.exp:
William Shakespeare is the greatest English dramatist. He is famous for the objective presentation of his deep knowledge about human psychology.
He was born on 23 April, 1564 AD and died on 23 April, 1616 AD.
His Birth place is Stratford Avon. He is often called the bard of Avon.
The Shakespearean period belongs to '1590-1616'. He wrotes 37 plays and 154 sonnets.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৮) Who is called a neo-classicist?
Daily Quiz.exp:
A neo-classicist though Ben Jonson wrote in the time when romantic mode of literature was prevalent.
Ben Jonson is called a neo-classicist because he followed the classical rules of drama: Every Man in His Humour, Every Man Out of His Humour.
His comedies are known as 'Comedy of Humors'.
His famous works are The Magnetic Lady, Volpone, The Silent Woman, The Alchemist, The Devil is an Ass etc.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ১৯) Which of the following novel is written by Daniel Defoe?
Daily Quiz.exp:
'Robinson Cruse' is a famous novel which is written by Daniel Defoe. His other famous novel is Captain Singleton.
The Double Dealer is written by William Congreve.
Pamela or Virtue Rewarded, the first English novel, is written by Samuel Richardson.
"Joseph Andrews", a novel by Henry Fielding, published in 1742. It was written as a reaction against Samuel Richardson's novel Pamela; or, Virtue Rewarded.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica.

Daily Quiz.question: ২০) Who is the writer of 'Euphues'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
John Lyly is a University Wit.
His famous works are Campaspe, Sapho and Phao, Midas, Euphues (a book that bears the embryo of English novel) etc.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ২১) Father of English Sacred Song -
Daily Quiz.exp:
Caedmon is the first known poet or earliest epic poet of English literature. He is also called Father of English Sacred Song.
He is the writer of Paraphrase.
Source: Encyclopedia Britannica and History of English Literature by Shetal Ghosh.

Daily Quiz.question: ২২) What is the Slogan of Neo-Classical period?
Daily Quiz.exp:
'Art for man's sake' is the slogan of Neo-Classical period.
'Art for art's sake' is the slogan of Romantic Period.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৩) 'The Tempest' by William Shakespeare is a-
Daily Quiz.exp:
William Shakespeare is the greatest English dramatist. He is mostly known for his plays. His last work is The Tempest. It is his famous comedy.
His notable comedies are As You Like It, The Comedy of Errors, Twelfth Night, The Taming of The Shrew, Mid Summer Night's Dream, The Two Gentleman of Verona, The Merry Wives of Windsor, The Winter's Tale, Cymbeline, Pericles, Prince of Tyre, The Two Nobel Kinsman, Much Ado About Nothing, Love's Labours Lost.
source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopedia of Britanncia.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৪) Who is a Cavalier poet?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Cavalier poet, any of a group of English gentlemen poets, called Cavaliers because of their loyalty to Charles I (1625–49) during the English Civil Wars, as opposed to Roundheads, who supported Parliament.
They were also cavaliers in their style of life and counted the writing of polished and elegant lyrics as only one of their many accomplishments as soldiers, courtiers, gallants, and wits.
The term embraces Richard Lovelace, Thomas Carew, Sir John Suckling, Edmund Waller, and Robert Herrick.

Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ২৫) 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard' was written by-
Daily Quiz.exp:
An Elegy Written in a Country Church Yard, a meditative poem written in iambic pentameter quatrains by Thomas Gray, published in 1751.
Source: Britannica.com

Daily Quiz.question: ২৬) ’Piers Plowman’ was written by-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Piers Plowman, a satirical poem, was written by William Langland.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৭) Which is the earliest epic in English literature?
Daily Quiz.exp:
Beowulf is the Earliest Epic in English literature (England). It is also the first monument in English literature.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৮) Which is the famous allegory in prose?
Daily Quiz.option1: ক) The Battle of the Books
Daily Quiz.option2: খ) The Way of The World
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Pilgrim's Progress, the famous allegory in prose, is written by John Bunyan.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

Daily Quiz.question: ২৯) Which period is called 'the Golden age of English literature'?
Daily Quiz.exp:
The Elizabethan Period is called 'the Golden age of English literature'.
Duration of Elizabethan Period is 1558 to 1603. The other titles of this age: Glorious Period of English literature, Golden Period of English Drama, A nest of singing birds.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.

Daily Quiz.question: ৩০) The first Lexicographer in English is-
Daily Quiz.exp:
Dr. Samuel Jonson is the Father of English dictionary. He is the first lexicographer in English.
His famous books are A Preface to Shakespeare, Rasselas: Prince of Abissinia, Life of the English Poets etc.
His famous poem is 'The Vanity of Human Wishes'.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Live MCQ Lecture.
